source.title: Constructing Interpretable Features from Compositional Neuron Groups
source.authors: O. Shafran; Atticus Geiger; Mor Geva

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent garbling or cutoff affecting the study.
record.tranche_reason: Applies a new feature-decomposition method to LLMs and reports results about neuron-composed features, their overlap, and their causal effects. It does not reproduce the toy-network method.
record.gate_note: The study reports SNMF feature detection, neuron overlap, hierarchy and causal-intervention results. Comparisons with SAEs and DiffMeans are not extracted as standalone rows where they only compare the paper's method with alternatives; the main-text steering comparison is presented graphically and its exact values are not stated. Results cited from other studies are not counted.
record.test_reason: Applies a dictionary-style decomposition (SNMF) to LLM MLP activations. It reports how often the recovered sparse neuron-combination features align with concepts (>75% positive detection scores) and that neurons are shared across features. This bears on V4 in a new setting. Most other results concern hierarchical composition of neuron groups, which no version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also claim SNMF features beat SAEs and DiffMeans on causal steering and match SAEs on detection. They argue SAE feature splitting reflects the model's neuron composition rather than being only a training artifact.
record.recipe_differences: Uses semi-nonnegative matrix factorization on LLM MLP activations, followed by feature and causal-steering evaluations; it does not use the original toy-network setup or test its sparsity-dependent geometric transitions.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported concept-detection performance varies by layer and model; increasing k generally improves it but has exceptions, including degradation at Gemma-2-2B layer 12. Early-layer steering has lower final scores, attributed to fluency sensitivity. The paper also reports performance variation across WTA sparsity settings and initialization strategies.

fits_no_version.finding: Semantically related features share a core neuron base that promotes all weekday tokens. Exclusive neurons promote their own day and suppress the others. Recursive SNMF parents cover their children's promoted tokens (coverage 0.37-0.47 vs 0.00-0.05 random).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron sharing across features in LLM MLPs reflects hierarchical compositional reuse of neuron groups, an account of multi-feature neurons distinct from capacity-driven superposition.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2025)
record.problems: The main feature benchmark uses k<500. The authors note reliance on LLM judges, with a human agreement check on 50 judged examples (Spearman ρ = 0.8, p < 10−4), but acknowledge possible prompt and evaluation sensitivity. Some hierarchy examples are manually selected, and the broad hierarchy test uses generated datasets and the study’s own SNMF-derived links.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3 steering comparisons across layers and methods were not extracted as separate rows: exact values are figure-only, and the reported comparison is primarily between the paper’s method and alternatives. Other figure-only trends and appendix method-selection/initialization comparisons were omitted because they do not add a separately stated result about the claim’s representation geometry.

untested.parts: No toy models, no feature-count vs dimension sweep, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
No test of capacity competition or of importance-dependent dedicated dimensions.
Argues neuron sharing reflects compositional reuse, but does not test polysemanticity in the absence of capacity pressure.
No test of SAE feature completeness, stability or canonicity. SAE comparisons are method-vs-method steering benchmarks.
Cites multi-dimensional weekday representations (Engels et al.) but does not test 1-D vs multi-D features.

missing.what: Per-layer concept-detection means (e.g. Llama random init: L0 2.99±1.55, L31 0.48±0.62) showing strong layer dependence of dictionary feature recovery
k-dependence of detection scores, including degradation with larger k at Gemma-2-2B layer 12

record.verdict_notes: The SNMF neuron sparsity is imposed by a winner-take-all operator (top 1% of neurons, 5% for GPT-2), so 'sparse neuron groups' partly reflects method design. Steering comparisons with SAEs (Fig. 3) are method benchmarks, are figure-only, and were not used for V5. Diversity rows (r13, r19) do not differ from random controls, contrary to the reader's supports label. V4 support is indirect: SNMF codes Y are nonnegative but not explicitly sparse.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, overcomplete sparse-feature sweep, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular-geometry test.
Does not test capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or a relation between feature importance and sharing.
Finds shared neuron groups but does not test whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure or whether it is evidence for superposition.
Tests SNMF-derived features and their neuron composition in LLMs; it does not establish that SAE features are a complete account of the representations.
Does not test completeness, stability, or canonical status of SAE features.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multi-dimensional feature representations.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-2B, and GPT-2 Small (aggregate as stated)
rows.operation_detail: Measured SNMF-feature concept detection as a log-ratio of activating- and neutral-sentence cosine scores.

conditions.value: multiple layers; aggregate statement across models and layers

rows.measure: Percentage of SNMF features with positive concept-detection scores
rows.note: The authors state that most SNMF features across layers and models have positive scores, meaning stronger activation for concept-related than neutral inputs. This is an aggregate textual result.
rows.check: Aggregate over Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-2B and GPT-2 Small at k=100. The baseline is neutral generated sentences, not 'not stated'. A minority of features score negative.

source_check.correct: Baseline: generated neutral sentences that do not exemplify the feature's concept. Detection score: log-ratio of mean maximum cosine similarities for activating versus neutral sentences.
source_check.problem: The neutral-sentence baseline is stated; recording it as not stated omits the comparison underlying positive detection scores.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Compared overlap in binarized top-activating-neuron sets for weekday features and randomly sampled features.

conditions.value: First seven features correspond to Monday through Sunday; remaining features randomly sampled

rows.measure: Shared neuron counts between feature pairs
rows.value: Weekday features had higher shared-neuron counts with one another; diagonal counts were increased; weekday/weekend group overlap was higher within groups; overlap with the remaining sampled features was described as little.
rows.note: The text describes the qualitative pattern; the figure contains the plotted counts. The study says weekday features share core neurons and also have distinct neurons.
rows.check: GPT-2 Small, recursive-SNMF time-units dataset. Shows neurons shared across features, i.e. distributed, multi-use neurons. Neuron sparsity within each feature is imposed by WTA (top 1-5%), so 'spread' is partly set by the method. Values are figure-only (Fig. 5).

rows.subject: GPT-2 Large
rows.operation_detail: Amplified the neuron base shared across weekday features and measured changes in weekday-token logits.

conditions.value: Amplify neuron base shared across all weekday MLP features
Change in logits for Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, in that order

rows.note: The authors interpret the increases for all weekday tokens as the shared neuron base encoding a high-level weekday concept.
rows.check: Causal effect of a shared neuron base on weekday logits in GPT-2 Large. This concerns hierarchical composition, not superposition or dictionary recovery. The model differs from the GPT-2 Small used in Fig. 5.

relationships.condition: SNMF (k=100-400) on MLP activations of Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-2B, GPT-2 Small
relationships.reason: >75% of recovered features detect their concept above neutral inputs (r1). Features share neuron subsets, so neurons serve multiple features (r2).
relationships.display_finding: Over 75% of recovered features detected their concept above neutral inputs, and features shared neuron subsets, so individual neurons served multiple features.

relation.reason: Concept detection and shared-neuron measurements bear directly on V4, beyond reporting the decomposition method's comparative steering performance.

tranche.reason: SNMF decomposition and neuron-sharing analyses provide results on distributed concept representations in pretrained LLM MLP activations, a new setting relative to the original toy models.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v2 dated 2 May 2026. Feature sparsity is imposed by winner-take-all truncation; the separate weekday causal interventions name GPT-2 Large, whereas the recursive-decomposition example names GPT-2 Small.

statements.correction: This study decomposes MLP activations using SNMF, yielding sparse linear combinations of neurons; its supporting results do not rely on ordinary SAE feature recovery.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SNMF feature detection across tested models and layers; weekday neuron-group interventions in GPT-2 Large; parent-child hierarchies in Llama-3.1 8B and Gemma-2 2B
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports concept-aligned SNMF features, shared and exclusive neuron groups with corresponding logit effects, and parent-child feature effects above unrelated-feature controls (r1-r11, r13, r15, r17, r19, r21).
